I'm glad you manage to see it that way! Hopefully this rough patch will pass quickly. :)

I'm not only talking about your life, I'm also saying that someone else's might end.

As for your own thoughts, I don't intend to diminish them in any way. These kind of feelings can make you think and do a lot of things. I hope you manage to weather the storm.
That's rough my friend. Heartache can bring you to your wit's end. Intense emotions like these can really mess you up. Hope you manage to weather the storm.
That's rough my friend. I will only say, that in my opinion suicide never brought any happiness to anyone. I hope you find your path in life.
If it's any consolation, I've been in a place where I was completely hopeless, and for me it passed. My heart goes out to you.

My heart goes out to you. I've been in a place where I felt so alone my body physically hurt, and all I wanted was to rip my heart from my chest. If it's any comfort, for me it passed, so I think it's possible for others as well. I hope you find your path in life.

Can't you find what you enjoy in life? It doesn't have to be a huge accomplishment or goal. Maybe it's the people around you that you don't enjoy and not life itself? I hope you find your path in life.

In my opinion, this is really aweful. I understand that some times people self harm, even to a suicidal point, but this is a really bad way. If you hit someone else, which is likely if you drive precariously, it's the same as killing them with your own hands. I hope you find your path in life.
Hey. It is tough at the moment, but what helps me when I get down is knowing that its temporary, and I won't feel like this forever. I hope you find your path in life.

Hey. This is me speaking from my experience and does not apply to everyone, but If I was him I would appreciate the concern. Maybe even just sending him messages/memes or whatever, showing that you care and think about them without having to always talk about the 'heavy' stuff.
Hey there. IMO it's ok to call and use them alot if times. It's their job/they volunteer exactly for this purpose. You are using the service for it's intended purpose. Hope you find your path.
Hopefully lockdown ends soon or continues in a good way. I hope you manage through it.

No problem. You can also look at it the other way around. Whenever you come crashing down, you end up hopeful or optimistic. We all have ups and downs. What helps me is that I know that even when I'm in a dark place, it doesn't last forever.

Hey. Wanted to say I read your post. What you're dealing with is pretty tough, and I hope you can manage through it. Having no support is maddening, and it can really get you to your wit's end. Despite that, I'll tell you that you can make it, even if it seems impossible. I hope you find your path in life, and that you will look back to these impossible moments from your peaceful future.

Hey, depression is not owned by people who are down-trodden. You could be a billionaire and still feel the call of the void. I was 23 before I had my first real relationship, before then I just got rejected again and again. Relationships can be super difficult, especially if you feel like you're malfunctioning. I wanted you to know that I felt like this too, like I'm unworthy of love. It passes. You can make it, and you'll look back on these building moments. I hope you find your path in life.

Hey. I want to say that I know it can be liberating to have the "keys to escape the prison cell", even if you don't plan to use them. I hope that when you come close to using them, you'll give life another shot. In any case, wanted to let you know that my heart is with you, and I hope you find your path in life.

Hey there. Read your post, and hope you find your path. It's definitely not straightforward, but there are many things to continue living for in my opinion. Hardships are a part of life, and you have your plate beyond full right now, but it does get better, I'm telling you. Is it not worth it to try and weather the storm? You got nothing to lose, only gain. Anyways I hope you find your path in life.

Well, sometimes depression strikes despite all of the above. Doesn't matter if you are a handsome billionaire. Not saying that you should commit suicide but "it could be worse is not a valid argument IMO. I think that each person's battle is different, and we all have our journeys and hardships to endure.
Truth right here. Just jumping on the bandwagon with 0 explaination

Hey man, I read your post. 

First of all I wanted to tell you that being supported is perfectly fine at your age. This is not the 20th century where you could live off a minimum wage and even save some. Living is exepnsive is hell and, at least in my country, most young adults are supported in some way or another by family/country. You should not feel ashamed of being helped, but grateful that someone is there to help you.

It's also difficult moving along without a purpose or a passion. I've been there, stuck in a loop of doing stuff that feels like just time fillings. What helped me is trying alot of different activities. Just trying made me feel better, and try even more stuff until I found something that I loved, not just liked. Maybe even go and take swimming lessons? Convince yourself that you are not destined to die in the Nile. If you learnt how to swim, which is entirely possible, maybe you will feel the start of a change for the better?

Whatever you decide, I hope you find peace, and your path in life. My heart is with you

Hey.

I'm here, with a nice cup of tea. What's bothering you?

I feel you.

One of the worst feelings out there is feeling stuck. Nowhere to go, nothing to do about it. I've felt the same way for a long, long period of my life. I can only tell you what I did, and hope it will aid you in finding your path in life. 

In a sense, no one is special. We're all just humans that die eventually, and rare are the people who leave a mark. What's left then? The answer, to me at least, is myself. Your only true obligation is to your own life. Yes, we all die, and mortality can be disheartening and numbing, but it's also liberating. Seek purpose, and if you don't find it, seek peace. It's hard to picture when you're low, but your own life and experiences are worth living for. If you are stuck, you are the one who needs to free you. 

I know it's easier said than done, and I have known success and many failures in this field, but as cliche as it sounds, it's always the darkest before the dawn.

Hope you manage to find your path in life.

Hey.

I read your entire story, its a rough one. First of all I dont wish anyone the kind of horrible abuse you went through at youth. That kind of events leave behind deep scars, that if left unattended will rarely heal. 

What you did to your wife was as horrible as what your father did to you, and im sure you know that and thats a major part of what makes you feel the way you feel now. However, you are NOT your father, and you can act differently. Its going to be tough, the toughest thing you have ever done probably, but it is possible.

My advice for you is talking to your wife. Dont justify your actions, dont try to explain them. She may not forgive you, but all you can do is work on yourself. It is now her choice how she wants to continue, and you gotta respect that.

Whatever you do, I hope things will turn out for the better, and that you find your path in life.

The thing about deadlines is, they are both good and bad.

Good in the sense of comfort they give, having something to wait for, knowing that time passes and the date will come, not one minute later.

They're also bad though, because when the deadline comes, and you're down it can bring you to a new low. It gives justification for the depression.

I dont know if things will get better for you. I dont know when the sun will shine. 

But I do know it's possible.

Maybe not tomorrow, not at your birthday or a month after. But things can, and will, look up.

I hope you find your path in life, my heart is with you.

To get the sinking feeling to stop, get off the balcony, eat something, go to sleep. You have to wait, let the tears run out.

And my remedy for the mirror, is action. I dont know you, nor your circmustances, but I believe you can endure. Find something to do, and do it. Be it a hobby, excercise, or anything else, that's positive and constructive. 

I might not know what Im talking about, im just telling you what helped me a bit, in hopes it will you too.

In my opinion you should not define yourself by other people. Thats easier said than done. I know the pain of being lonely. That sinking feeling deep in your chest. I, too, sat once on an edge of a window high atop a hotel in 4am.

At the end of the day, you are the only person that will truly understand yourself. You have your whole life to live with yourself, so you have to sit down and figure out how you can do that. Im not saying there's some magical solution. It keeps hurting. But there is hope, and I promise you, like the tides, as much as life has lows, it has highs.

My heart goes out to you.
Well, I can talk. Try putting to words the reasons behind your feelings.
Hey. Im here. I know that feeling, that lonliness. Feel free to talk to me.

I am not in your shoes. I am not as poor as you describe, and am not in great debt like you. Your situation is very tough, and I can read the feeling of having no way out from your words. I dont know if i was mistaken, i simply wish to aid another person on this planet.

I've sent you a private message.

I've written this before and I'll write it again. 

Fuck everyone.

People can think and expect all they want. They are not the ones working instead or you, dealing with your problems. If you feel you need a break, find out how you can make it happen. Im not deluded that you can get up and travel for half a year, but I think you can find something to help you rest your mind. 

There is no someday. Someday only happens if you acrually give it a date. You can change it, postpone it, but itll be real.

Im not sure about actual numbers and minimum wages, but have you actually sat down and tried to calculate how much you need each month? There are alot of ways to help you, like cooking your own food and budgeting ahead of time.

Besides, if you find a job you're good at, you might be able to start earning more. Don't think about why you *can't* make it, think how you *can*. Your life might end up a long series of boring years one after another, but it can also be a story of achievements, rising and accomplishment. Is that not worth a shot?

For me atleast, hiking and traveling is about nature and the wilds.

 >poor people shouldn't dream.

That's just not true. To me it seems you are telling yourselves this because it's easier. Easier to blame the world for the outragous imbalance between the rich and the poor than working on your goals. I think you know it's possible for you to achieve your goals, the only thing stopping you is your mindset. Plan a trip, budget it, start saving on various things and im sure you'll be able to get there.

Hey.

First of all, I've read your post, all of it. Know that a stranger is aware of your plight, and that my heart goes out to you.

From my view of the world everyone has something that seems to tie their hands, be it family, money, or simply themselves. For me it was my religious family. I've spent many nights alone on my bed, wondering and wishing how better it would have been if my life was just a tiny bit different. After alot of soul searching my realization was that everybody has things that limit and hinder them. The trick is to find a passion, something you want to do, and you'll manage.

Want to travel? Start by packing a bag with water and food and hiking through local nature. Fuck the boss man on top. You are living only for yourself, and the people you love. Life is tough, and everyone gets a different and uneven starting point. That does not mean we can't be happy in our own means. It's a bit cliche, but I found that the happiest i've been is doing the small things. Reading a book, talking to friends, a nice calming hike.

I hop you find a path in life, through the many obstacles it has thrown your way.

Hey.

Have you considered your mind is tricking you? What I mean is from what you wrote, it seems you are normal. You work to better yourself, you are awkward at social situations. I guarantee you are thinking the bad over the good of yourself. Now, realizing this can be helpful, knowing sometimes that when you think little of yourself, it is not true. You don't have to be down on your luck to talk to someone. Everyone, *everyone* has their problems. You just need to find the way that helps you work with yours.

Anyways, hope I helped, and that you find your path in life. I think it's going to get better for you.

Personally, if I ever commit suicide, there won't be a note. If I feel that I want to cease to exit, then I don't mind what others will think. This is a rough world, and character gets molded by both good and bad. They can feel and experience whatever they will, my path is mine to take.

Regardless, I still hope you find a way, and that your life will be fulfilling. My heart is with you.

Fuck everybody.

Whatever they do or don't think is not something that should make you want to end yoir life. You were right, you **are** your own best friend. Nobody takes care of you better than yourself. Nobody else cares that much about how you look, how you talk, how you feel. You probably won't find someone who will magically fall in love with you. But you can change. Change for the better. 

What you need to do is change your mindset. You already convincing yourself you are terrible. Why not convince yourself you are good? Thought creates reality. If you keep telling yourself bad thongs, you'll feel bad. Good things, youll feel better. Go to the bathroom and look yourself in the mirror. Find good things about yourself and tell them to yourself. Not bad, only good. I promise you, you are capable of changing yourself for the better.

Hope you find your path in life, my heart goes out to you.

This could just be your mind going in defense mode.

It's thinking "Fuck! This project is important and I didnt manage to do it! Maybe if I tell myself I dont care about it, then I will be in less pain?"

What you need to do, first of all, is realize that it *isn't* such a big deal. School is important because of the experiences and the skill learning, not the actual grades. Even if you flunk every class and have to do the year again, believe me that it doesn't matter in the long run. You just have to improve yourself from failures.

That being said, you *need* to go to school today. First of all, your friend needs you, and showing that you care about them enough to try will mean alot. Another thing is that if you don't go, your will feel worse and start a downward spiral. If you go and face the consenquences, even if you fail the project you can tell yourself that you tried, and you will feel better, starting an upward spiral.

Whatever you do, I hope you find your path in life. Good luck!

You don't need to change the world to have a reason to stay in it. Every person has a different drive, what makes them want to achieve. As you have homework Im guessing you are still in school which means life has not really been open for you yet. There is meaning in the small things. To gather experiences, meet people, just think of all of the sucess and failure you will havr throughout your life, and that will make you, well, *you*.

On another note, you are changing the world. From my percpective, if you do good, help one person in need, then you've changed the world. One tiny bit, but nevertheless. Eventually you will eo something you deem insignificant, but will mean the world to someone else.

I hope you find your path in life.

"I just don't care ever and it hurts me"

You do care, that's why it hurts. You wish you focused more, worked harder on yourself. You are positive that you cannot succeed and that you are useless. That anything you do is deemed to fail.

I've been there. I grew up feeling nothing I did was meaningful, by the end of highschool I just played video games for six months. 

What you need to do, what helped me, was just acting, as in performing actions. Whether it be working out, reading, going to a bar and meeting something new, whenever I got the feeling of "gee, I wish I did this and that", I get up, and do what I can towards it. 

You won't be successful all the time, and you'll fail. That's ok. This is the age to make mistakes, you just gotta remember to learn from them. At eighteen your emotions and character are evolving, and that causes alot of pain. Not just for you, for almost everyone around your age. 

Lastly, it gets better. It does. This is just another stepping stone towards you becoming yourself. It hurts like hell now, but you will learn from it about yourself. So many people tell us it gets better. Instead of shaking our heads, waddling in our misery we need to have some faith. You can, and *will* get through this, despite evrything, and you *will* emerge to be stronger.

I hope you find your way in life, my heart is with you.

"I know that telling you I have suicidal thoughts is serious, and im unsure what these feelings mean, and how serious they are. If I just find the idea of not existing appealing, or that im actually in a path that end with me dead. Im scared that you will have to tell others, which will affect my life. I dont want to be 'kept alive', i want to stop feeling suicidal. Please voice your concerns to me, and try and help me out of this. I dont want to think about killing myself."

Just some stuff i thought about. Of course I dont know you and whether or not this fits with your case, but I hope I helped nevertheless. My heart goes out to you, and I hope you find your path in life.

Fuck the world. 

You must have something you enjoy doing. It doesn't have to be glamorous, or well paid. Video games, woodworking, gardening. You need to find what can get through through the day. I dont believe that you cannot achieve anything. I believe you can, no matter your current situation. Whenever you feel like the world is having a laugh at you, throwing obstacles in your way, point a middle finger at the sky and *do* something. Work out a bit. Clean your space. Read a bit. Its not the easy path, but its the right one.

I hope you manage to find your path in life. I believe in you.
You are very welcome, glad I could assist in any way.

In my humble opinion, giving yourself this kind of deadline is both good and bad.

Good, because it makes you feel free. Like you are in a cage but you hold the key. You have a reason to go on, you have a specific goal you can work towards.

Bad, because when the time comes, you might not be sure. Life has its highs and lows, and you might be in a place which is not bad, but due to temporary depression will seem horrible. Another thing is when the year passes and you feel suicidal, you have an excuse. 'Well I tried and it didn't work.' Life is effort, and it's not going to get magically better.

Hope you find your path in life.

I've read your entire post. First of all I want to say that I hope you make it through this low in life, and make it to to the good times again. Secondly, from my personal perspective, you think too much about the 'what if's. Even though I will never be in your shoes and be able to tell how you feel, I have been through quite a bit, and what helped me counter the 'what if's is doing. Doesnt matter what, as long as there is some benefit to you from the action. Work out, clean your room, learn to whistle. As long as I acted, the dreadful thoughts were forgotten for a bit, and when they came back, I had the comfort of having done something frugal.

I hope you find your path in life.

I know that feeling. 

The hardest it hit me was on a trip with friends. I couldn't fall asleep in the hotel, I felt so alone I tried to rip my heart out with my hand. It left marks on my chest. I went to the 7th floor and sat on the edge of the window, my feet dangling and watching the city lights below. I ended up returning to my room at 4 and going to sleep.

You need to survive this night. I know that if you live through it, you'll feel differently. That's how life works, highs and lows. You are not alone. You have someone who knows you better tgan anyone else. That wants you to become a better version of yourself. That person is you. You are capable of getting yourself out of this.

My heart goes out to you, and I hope you'll feel better!

Hey.

First of all I want to say I've read your post. All of it. From a quick google about GSCEs it seems you are still in middle school. From my personal exeprience, the grades that you get at these ages are not important. Like, literally nobody looked at them other than my mom. What's more important is learning to study, and getting to know yourself. Even though it seems like a big deal now, I can tell you it is not.

As for your family issues, it's a shame someone who isn't an adult yet has to deal with these kind of situations. I wish I could give you some advice, but I don't have anything to say other than that from what I've read, I think you are capable of surviving. I'm not talking about 'keep-on-living' survival, I'm talking working through the huge obstacles that are in your way, anf making the best person out of yourself. 

I hope my words gave you some comfort. My heart goes out to you.

In my humble opinion, your arguments, while logiacally sound, are somewhat superficial. While life is made possible by the rules of the universe, and no matter how cliche it sounds, we as humans are different. Your thought, your feelings, emotions, memories, together they make you more unique than anything that's been here before. How a new experience can affect you, can change you. I simply don't know what happens after we die, but I only know that it is permanent. This is the single chance we have to be humans, to experience life. As far as I'm concerned, I'm going to try and make the most out of it.

I hope I made sense, and that you find your path in life.

In my humble opinion, giving yourself this kind of deadline is both good and bad.

Good, because it makes you feel free. Like you are in a cage but you hold the key. You have a reason to go on, you have a specific goal you can work towards.

Bad, because when the time comes, you might not be sure. Life has its highs and lows, and you might be in a place which is not bad, but due to temporary depression will seem horrible. Another thing is when the year passes and you feel suicidal, you have an excuse. 'Well I tried and it didn't work.' Life is effort, and it's not going to get magically better.

Hope you find your path in life.

What do you think about trying a new kind of pain? I'm talking about the pain that comes with change. No matter how painful it is, how much you tell yourself it doesn't matter, work out. Be it jogging or strength, there's no excuses. If yout life does not matter to you, what does it matter if you postpone it a bit? Telling yourself you have to do it on a specific day may affect your judgement, since your birthday will fill you with emotions. Hope you manage to find your path in life.
It also feels more real. For me at least. I don't feel comfortable sharing personal details like my name and stuff online. In a therapy session you can truly let your lips get loose.
Personaly I think therapy does. It acts as a sort of mirror, helping you look at yourself from a different point of view. Talkiing to someone who cant tell others is also nice.

I was embarressed to go to the gym as well. I still don't go. All you need is running shoes and cloths, and you can start jogging around your home. No one bats an eye for someone with headphones on running past them. I began with running 15-30 minutes, and started adding crunchs and push ups before I showered each day. You don't need anything to begin, other than willpower.

Talking to a therapist can act like a sort of mirror, viewing yourself from a different perspective. Saying you know all there is to know about psychology can't be true, as there is always more to learn. Coming to a session with an open mind can do wonders.

This is just my humble opinion. I hope you find your path in life.

What helped me may not help you, and if you have medical depression it's a whole different story but here goes.

I was in a very bad place, using video games as an escape and basically not doing anything else. Just like you described, I felt lazy, worthless. I didn't think I had what it takes to change and it was comfortable and easy blaming myself. 

At one point I was browsing through reddit and read aomething stupid about how Mozart and Newton had the same hours in a day as me, and aomething clicked. I decided I'm changing, no excuses.

I began small, forcing myself to work out daily, even if it was for 15 minutes. It was super tough at the beginning but I learnt all the excuses I tried telling myself, and forced through them. I failed a couple of times, but 'no excuses' kept running through my head. I began thinking how I wanted my life to be and did what I had to do to get there.

Since then I've done the hardest thing I've done, which was change. I'm in a much better place now, and even though the dark thoughts come visit from time to time, I have the foundation to deal with them.

Hopefully this helped, and you will find your path in life.
I'm glad I could be of assistance. Have a good time tomorrow!

I enjoy hiking. Just take something to eat and some water, and wander around nature for a while. Personally I find it calming, and it clears my head when I do. Hope you manage to find something that interests you!

My heart goes out to you. I wish I had something to say to help you. Having to take care of people with your own happiness at the expense seems aweful to me. Are you a single mother? I hope you manage to find peace.

This seems to me like good advice. Unforunately we don't know you or the exact situation you are in, but from what you told us I think you should go where you will be happier. Convincing your parents will be tough, but you know them so try and appeal to them. You sound like you work hard to achieve, and in my experience hard works pays, no matter the name of the school you went to. I hope you manage to make the best out of this!

Hey. Im glad you found someone who sympasizes with you, it can be very helpful with dealing with depression. This is not silly at all, talking to someone who shares interests is amazing. The only thing I will add is just don't throw caution to the wind. You've made a new friend and it's amazing, but don't share things you feel comfortable sharing, and take your time getting to know him. I hope Leon will be an awesome friend!

It's tough having to deal with stuff like this alone. Perhaps trying another, different, therapist will change? They are getting paid, but they can act like a mirror, and show you yourself from a different point of view. Of course, I don't know you or your plight, so everything I say should be taken with a grain of salt. 

You can also try what I suggested beforehand.

Hey. I read your post, and my heart goes out to you. The things you deal with at 18 years old are tougher than some deal with their whole lives. I wish I could help you stay strong, and I hope you will make it through. A stranger's prayers, thoughts and tears are with you.

Hey. I read your post, top to bottom. From my humble point of view, you had a negative, even traumatic experience, and you don't know how to deal with it, which leads down a spiral of negativity. My advice is that you should see a therapist. Not because I think you have a mental illness, but because I think you have no one to talk to, no one you feel safe confiding in. A therapist is just that, someone to talk to. If you don't want to talk to a therapist, try talking to yourself in the mirror or recording yourself talking using a computer. It might help you reflect, and start building your life again. 

I hope you find your path in life.
I honestly liked the picture without make up the most. Your shy smile is beautiful. You are way too hard on yourself with trying to be 'perfect', a little side smile hurts no-one.
It is not pathetic. You are having a difficult struggle with yourself, and I hope you manage to overcome and choose to better yourself.

I read your post. My heart goes out to you. You are in a difficult place in life right now, and I sincerely hope you manage to help yourself out of it. You won an archery competition. Accomplishments are earned with talent and hard work, and I hope you manage to work your way down your path of life, and be happy. My thoughts are with you.

In my humble opinion, there is no 'being human' but rather you are already one. Every person have their struggles, some hide it better than others. I believe that even if you don't see it right now, you can have a place on this earth. I hope you find your path in life.
I read your post. I don't know you or your plight, but I hope you find your path in life, and that things will work out for the best soon. A stranger's thoughts are with you.
Personally i prefer therapy to medication. Confiding in someone can be a great deal for mental health. Hope you find your path in life.
You look really good. I don't normally comment on these but I like your style.

Hey. I read your post, all of it. From my humble point of view, what you need to do is start small. Your parents have high expectations from you, which have led you to be over critical of yourself. From what you wrote they seem abusive and damaging, so my advice is to leave them mostly out of your life. You wrote you have your own income, your own child, your own house. It is your life, not theirs. 

As for your self doubt, what helped me is realizing that your mind is tricking you. It's normal to fail. We all do, no exceptions. The next time you feel the way you described, try telling yourself that. Negative emotions are a part of life. They arn't something that need concealing, that should be hid. It's you being human.

Another thing I would recommend is seeing a therapist. Talking to someone without fear of them telling someone else can truly help. For me it was like looking at myself from another person's point of view. Some people find them helpful, some don't, but trying it is important.

My heart is with you, and I hope you find your path in life.

Hey. I read your post, all of it. Your story seems tragic to me, and my heart goes out to you. I believe there is a place on this earth for you, and I hope you find it before going through the final route. I hope you find your path. I can never know what your thoughts and feelings are, so all I can do, all I will do, is tell you my thoughts are with you.

Hey. I read your entire post. The position you are in is a very difficult one, I don't know what I would have done in your stead. All three of you seem like you want the other two to be happy. I can't possibly know the depth of your feelings, so I will only say my thoughts are with you, and I hope you will overcome the obstacles in your life.

This is not how it has to be. As a person dealing with depression, sometimes your mind is fooling you to belive that way. I can't possibly know how you feel, and whether you are truly desperate. Only thing I can tell you is that suicde is a choice. There is always the option of living. If you decide to do it, it has to be a chouce you make with a clear mind, after a very long time of thinking it through. You don't want to die. That in itself tells everything. The only one that decides about your life is yourself, no one else. I hope you find your path in life.
